service: An Amazon S3 table represents a structured dataset consisting of tabular data in Apache Parquet format and related metadata. This data is stored inside an S3 table as a subresource. All tables in a table bucket are stored in the Apache Iceberg table format. Through integration with the Amazon Web Services Glue Data Catalog you can interact with your tables using Amazon Web Services analytics services, such as Amazon Athena and Amazon Redshift. Amazon S3 manages maintenance of your tables through automatic file compaction and snapshot management. For more information, see Amazon S3 table buckets.

operations.CompleteTableMigration:
Completes the migration of a table. The table's most recent migration must be in the succeeded, failed or cancelled state. After you complete the migration, you can't sync the table again, and you can write to and maintain the table as you do any other table: compaction starts, and unreferenced file removal follows the table bucket's configuration. You can't undo this operation. Calling it again for the same table returns a ConflictException.

Permissions

  • You must have the s3tables:CompleteTableMigration permission to use this operation.

operations.StartTableMigration:
Starts migrating an Amazon Web Services Glue Data Catalog table into a new table in a table bucket. The migration runs asynchronously: this operation returns the migration ID and its initial state, and you track progress with GetTableMigration.

The namespace must already exist, and a table with the specified name must not. The migration creates the table during planning and commits data to it as it runs. Until you call CompleteTableMigration, you can read the table but you can't write to it. If the migration fails or is cancelled, the table and the data already committed to it remain.

The migration first checks the source and the destination, and writes the table compatibility and object compatibility reports to the bucket that you specify in migrationOutput. If you set reviewMigrationPlan to true, the migration waits in the pendingReview state so that you can review the reports, and continues only when you call UpdateTableMigration with requestedState set to queued. If you don't continue or cancel the migration within 30 days, the migration fails. Otherwise it continues to migrate the data, and writes the object migration report when the migration ends. If planning fails, the migration writes no object migration report.

Permissions

  • You must have the s3tables:StartTableMigration permission to use this operation.

  • You must have the iam:PassRole permission on the role that you specify in roleARN, with a condition that allows passing it to migration.s3tables.amazonaws.com. The associated resource is the table bucket.

  • If destinationTable specifies SSE-KMS encryption, you must have the kms:DescribeKey and kms:GenerateDataKey permissions on the KMS key. You must also grant the S3 Tables maintenance principal access to the key. For more information, see Permissions requirements for S3 Tables SSE-KMS encryption.
operations.SyncTableMigration:
Migrates the changes in the source table since the previous start or sync, such as added and deleted source objects, into the destination table. The sync runs asynchronously: this operation returns the migration ID of the sync and its initial state, and you track progress with GetTableMigration.

A sync uses the source, destination and data migration settings of the table's migration, and plans the work and writes its reports in the same way as StartTableMigration. You can sync after a start or sync that succeeded, failed or was cancelled, if an earlier start or sync of the table has a valid plan (hasValidPlan). You can't sync a table while a start or sync is in progress for it, and you can sync a table until you call CompleteTableMigration for it. If a source object that an earlier migration migrated has since been overwritten, the sync fails.

Permissions

  • You must have the s3tables:SyncTableMigration permission to use this operation.

  • You must have the iam:PassRole permission on the role that you specify in roleARN, with a condition that allows passing it to migration.s3tables.amazonaws.com. The associated resource is the table.

Permissions

You must have the s3tables:UpdateTableMetadataLocation permission to use this operation.
operations.UpdateTableMigration:
Requests a state change for a migration. Identify the migration by its migrationId or by the tableARN of its destination table.

Set requestedState to queued to continue a migration in the pendingReview state; the migration moves to queued or migrating. Set it to cancelled to cancel a migration in the new, planning, pendingReview, queued or migrating state; the migration moves to cancelling, finishes the work in progress, and then ends in the cancelled state, or in the failed state if any objects failed to migrate. Data that the migration already committed stays in the destination table.

Permissions

  • You must have the s3tables:UpdateTableMigration permission to use this operation.

FindingCategory.base:
The category of a compatibility report finding, by what you change to fix it. Valid values:

  • access - A permission or a request setting. You don't need to change the source.

  • metadata - The Amazon Web Services Glue table definition, or properties of a source object, such as its size, storage class, encryption or Parquet types.

  • data - The contents of a source object, such as a partition value that can't be read, an object overwritten after an earlier migration, or a corrupt file.

  • internal - An internal error in S3 Tables. Retry the migration, and contact Amazon Web Services Support if the error persists.

refs.ReportOverview$invalidFindings: For the compatibility reports, the number of blocking findings in each category. The object compatibility report counts each blocked object once, under its most severe finding. Categories with no blocking findings are left out.

GlueTableSource.base: An Amazon Web Services Glue Data Catalog table to migrate. The table must be an external Apache Hive table whose data is stored as Parquet in a general purpose bucket in the same account and Region as the table bucket. Views, transactional (ACID) tables, tables in an open table format such as Apache Iceberg, and tables registered with Amazon Web Services Lake Formation can't be migrated. If the table can't be migrated, the migration fails, and the table compatibility report lists the reason.

refs.SourceConfiguration$glueTable: An Amazon Web Services Glue Data Catalog table to migrate. If the table can't be migrated, the migration fails, and the table compatibility report lists the reason.

refs.DestinationTable$schema: The schema of the table to create. If you don't specify a schema, the migration infers it from the source table, with every column optional. A schema that you specify must include every partition column of the source table. It can leave out other columns only if unmatchedSourceFieldsPolicy is drop. A struct column must have the same fields as the source column. Column default values aren't supported. If you mark a column as required, every source object must have a value for it: an object with a null value in a required column fails to migrate. The destination table is partitioned in the same way as the source table. To specify fields in icebergSortOrder, you must specify a schema.
refs.IcebergMetadata$schemaV2: The schema for an Iceberg table using the V2 format. Use this property to define table schemas that include nested or complex data types such as struct, list, or map, in addition to primitive types. MigrationFailureCode.base: The reason a migration failed. Each code names the cause, or the report that lists the findings.

refs.MigrationFailureReason$code:
The failure code. It names the cause or the report that lists the findings. Valid values:

  • rolePermissions - S3 Tables couldn't assume the migration role, or the role doesn't have a permission that the migration needs. detail is the role ARN.

  • sourcePermissions - The migration role couldn't read the Amazon Web Services Glue table or the source objects. detail names the table (database.table) or the source bucket.

  • destinationPermissions - The migration role couldn't write to the table bucket or the report bucket. detail names the bucket.

  • resourceNotFound - A resource that you specified doesn't exist, such as the Amazon Web Services Glue table or the source bucket. detail names it.

  • sourceNotSupported - The source table can't be migrated, for example because it is empty, has too many objects, or has columns or partitions that can't be migrated. The table compatibility report lists the findings.

  • tableCompatibilityReport - The migration couldn't create the destination table, for example because a table with that name already exists or the KMS key can't be used. For a sync, the destination table changed after the previous migration. The table compatibility report lists the finding.

  • objectCompatibilityReport - Some source objects can't be migrated, for example because they are archived, or because they were overwritten after an earlier migration migrated them. The object compatibility report lists them.

  • objectMigrationReport - Some source objects failed to migrate. The object migration report lists them and the cause for each.

  • reportBucketNotSupported - The report bucket can't receive the migration's reports, for example because it is in a different Region than the table bucket.

  • internalError - S3 Tables encountered an internal error. Retry the migration, and contact Amazon Web Services Support if the error persists.

MigrationFailureDetail.base: The resource that the failure applies to, such as the role ARN, the Amazon Web Services Glue table (database.table) or a bucket. For sourceNotSupported, the reason that the source isn't supported.

refs.MigrationFailureReason$detail: The resource that the failure applies to, such as the role ARN, the Amazon Web Services Glue table (database.table) or a bucket. For sourceNotSupported, the reason that the source isn't supported, such as EMPTY_TABLE. This value isn't returned for the report codes or for internalError.

refs.GetTableMigrationResponse$failureReason: The reason that the migration failed. refs.GetTableMigrationResponse$state:
The state of the migration. Valid values:

  • new - S3 Tables accepted the request.

  • planning - The migration is checking the source table, its objects and the destination for compatibility, and writing the compatibility reports.

  • pendingReview - Planning finished, and the migration waits for you to continue or cancel it with UpdateTableMigration.

  • queued - The migration is waiting to start migrating data.

  • migrating - The migration is running the plan from the planning state: it copies data and commits it to the destination table. A migration reaches this state only if hasValidPlan is true.

  • succeeded - Every planned object migrated.

  • failed - The migration failed. Check failureReason for the cause.

  • cancelling - You cancelled the migration, and it is finishing the work in progress.

  • cancelled - The migration is cancelled.

A migration ends in the succeeded, failed or cancelled state. You can cancel it until it ends.

refs.MigrationSummary$state:
The state of the migration. Valid values:

  • new - S3 Tables accepted the request.

  • planning - The migration is checking the source table, its objects and the destination for compatibility, and writing the compatibility reports.

  • pendingReview - Planning finished, and the migration waits for you to continue or cancel it with UpdateTableMigration.

  • queued - The migration is waiting to start migrating data.

  • migrating - The migration is running the plan from the planning state: it copies data and commits it to the destination table. A migration reaches this state only if hasValidPlan is true.

  • succeeded - Every planned object migrated.

  • failed - The migration failed. Check failureReason for the cause.

  • cancelling - You cancelled the migration, and it is finishing the work in progress.

  • cancelled - The migration is cancelled.

refs.MigrationPolicies$unmatchedSourceFieldsP:
The migration policy for a source field that has no matching column in the destination schema. Valid values:

  • fail - Fails the migration. This is the default.

  • drop - Leaves source columns that the destination schema doesn't have out of the destination table, and doesn't migrate source objects outside the Amazon Web Services Glue table's partition locations.

A destination schema that leaves out a partition column or a field of a struct column fails the migration under either value.
